If you decide to use workshop gear that handles heat, be ready to pay what it costs. Unlike ordinary weapons, which only need to be sharper and sturdier, weapons that give off heat need all sorts of precautions so that their wielder is not caught in that heat.
Of course, weapons that simply spew fire at random and fabrics that resist burning are easy to come by. But a weapon that lets its user finely control exactly as much heat as they want, at the moment they want, and a fabric that blocks the heat itself usually cost a great deal, and you must not neglect the effort of learning to use them.
If you do invest that money and time, there will be that much more work that needs you.

The reason for using this weapon, which looks like a suitcase or an instrument case, is clear. First, to blend into everyday life. A weapon that is complex and unwieldy in combat is, precisely because of that inefficiency, more likely not to be recognized as a weapon at all.
Second, the storage capacity that the suitcase shape itself provides. For that reason, weapons shaped to hold things inside are actively used by the Devyat' Association.
Despite these strengths, though, it is not well regarded among those who handle workshop gear. You often hear things like "they'd have gotten stronger if they had put the time spent on this weapon into another one," or "it's gear for modern Fixers who only care about looking cool."
When you meet someone wielding such difficult gear, the fact that they are a high-ranking Fixer or a senior syndicate member... paradoxically means something else. That is why, in the workshops, this gear is called not a suitcase but a coffin. And coffins always come with butterflies.
※Unlocked at Uptie Ⅱ; active while deployed in battle
